clue.text: Inexpensive pile acquired by company

indicators.note: the pile is taken in by the company, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a heap is a pile

explanation.surface: A cheap house has been bought up by a firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile' looks like a grand house; here it simply means a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: something cheap and cheerful, bought for little money.

clue.text: Many a holidaymaker here affected by said vision?

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected or exaggerated in manner

indicators.note: said signals that the word for vision is heard rather than written

parts.note: sight is the faculty of vision

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether holidaymakers are swayed by some spoken vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a pitch for tents or caravans is where many holidaymakers stay.

clue.text: Odd quote about a bishop keeling over

indicators.note: in a down clue, keeling over turns the whole assembly upside down, so it reads from the bottom
the quote goes round the other letters, so they sit inside it

parts.note: to quote is to cite
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A strange remark about a churchman toppling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeling over' suits a down clue: CITARRE, read upwards, becomes the answer. Right Reverend is the formal style of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: odd behaviour is unpredictable, irregular, out of the ordinary.

clue.text: After giving birth, plan a tot's needs to have development

indicators.note: the letters need developing into a new form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the S of the possessive counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: Once the baby arrives, planning the toddler's needs must evolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have development' tells you to rearrange PLAN A TOTS; 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical term: the period following childbirth is described as this, as in the depression some mothers suffer.

clue.text: Guide unhappy in moment of truth

parts.note: to show someone the way is to guide them
down means depressed or unhappy

explanation.surface: A guide feeling miserable at a decisive moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a decisive confrontation that settles matters is a moment of truth.

clue.text: Agony over boundary reportedly hit very hard and extremely fast

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another means it stands above it

parts.note: hell is a state of agony

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for a boundary is heard, not spelt

parts.note: in cricket a boundary hit along the ground scores four runs
to leather is to thrash or beat hard

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: the bowler's agony as the batsman smashes a boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a 'boundary' is a shot reaching the edge of the field, scoring four (or six); 'over' also looks like cricket but just places HELL on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: going at breakneck speed, recklessly fast, originally of riders whipping horses.

clue.text: Female has week visiting country

parts.note: Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A woman spends a week on a trip abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an adult female human.

clue.text: Performing in two legs

parts.note: ON is the leg side in cricket
a stage is a leg of a journey

explanation.surface: A performer doing a turn on two legs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the 'on' side is also called the leg side, so one leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an actor in front of the audience during a show is performing.

clue.text: Steal the Spanish piece

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An order to steal a Spanish gun or artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' looks like a gun or artwork; it is a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the US five-cent coin is a piece of money of this name.

clue.text: 'Masquerade: class band', flyer broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A flyer advertising a masked party with a classy band.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a masquerade is a party where guests come in costume and masks.

clue.text: Materials used to portray pond plant

indicators.note: the letters are put to use in depicting something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist chooses materials to paint a pond plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Hippuris, an aquatic plant with whorled leaves, grows in ponds.

clue.text: Greek character faithfully reproduced songs?

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sic marks a quotation copied exactly, errors and all

explanation.surface: A Greek figure's songs copied faithfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by question mark: songs are one kind of what composers write and bands play.

clue.text: Hellish poorly? No end, having caught a sunburn

indicators.note: the shortened word catches the other letters inside it
the last letter of the word for poorly is dropped

parts.note: to be poorly is to be sick
a tan is the bronzing of skin from the sun

explanation.surface: Someone feeling dreadful, sunburnt with no let-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end' leaves SIC; 'poorly?' with its question mark looks like the definition, but 'Hellish' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: of the devil, and so fiendish or infernal.

clue.text: To cool food, such may be blown

parts.note: to fan is to cool with moving air
fare is food and drink

explanation.surface: Advice on blowing on food to cool it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'such may be blown': trumpets blow this flourish, and the surface's blowing on food misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a flourish of trumpets is played by blowing brass instruments.

clue.text: Understood tense account given by Italian

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
IT is short for Italian, as in gin and it (Italian vermouth)

explanation.surface: A tense statement from an Italian, understood by all.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: implied without being stated, understood without words.

clue.text: In document, called mad

indicators.note: the word for called goes inside the document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
rang means telephoned or called

explanation.surface: Someone named in a document as insane.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unhinged, insane, out of one's mind.

clue.text: What a stall on the pier may sell — book matches?

definitions.text: What a stall on the pier may sell

parts.note: a novel is a book
ties are drawn matches, or games in a cup draw

explanation.surface: A seaside stall's wares: books and matches?
explanation.definitionFit: Description: seaside piers have stalls selling trinkets and small gimmicky items.

clue.text: Arrive after month crossing heart of large US state

indicators.note: the arriving word is placed after the rest
the month straddles the central letter, which ends up inside it

parts.note: May is a month

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: to land is to arrive

explanation.surface: Reaching a big American state a month later.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the original thirteen states, with Baltimore and Annapolis.

clue.text: Sweet spot at the centre?

definitions.meaning: a hard, round, striped peppermint sweet sold in Britain
the centre of a target in darts or archery

explanation.surface: The sweet spot dead in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a peppermint boiled sweet popular in Britain, and the middle of a dartboard or target.

clue.text: Out of bed, drunk is on edge

parts.note: to be up is to be out of bed
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone up after a drunken night is jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tense, anxious, nervy.

clue.text: 'Twelfth Night' character explosive? Not half, involving leader in Illyria

indicators.note: the shortened word wraps round the leading letter
only the first half of the word for explosive is used

parts.note: volatile means liable to explode

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean character described as explosive, set in Illyria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps VOLA, half of VOLATILE; 'involving' puts I, the leader of Illyria, inside. Illyria is the play's setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the heroine shipwrecked in Illyria who disguises herself as Cesario.

clue.text: Eccentric hoarding silver? Shock horror!

indicators.note: the eccentric word stores the silver inside it

parts.note: outre means unconventional or eccentric
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An oddball found stockpiling silver, to general horror.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a public outcry, the shocked indignation that greets a scandal.

clue.text: Savoury from Greek island area

parts.note: Samos is an island in the eastern Aegean

explanation.surface: A tasty snack from a region of a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fried triangular pastry with a spiced filling is a savoury snack.

clue.text: Employed by rival paper? Now and then

parts.note: to work at a firm is to be employed by it
The Times is a rival paper to the Daily Telegraph

explanation.surface: A journalist working for a competitor, now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is a British national newspaper competing with the Telegraph, where this clue appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: occasionally, from time to time.

clue.text: Landed estate's custom, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word for custom is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a manner is a customary way of doing something

explanation.surface: The traditions of a country estate are discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a country house with its lands, held by a lord.

clue.text: Writer cast lots in play

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed in the word for play

parts.note: to toy is to play

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters fall in a new order

explanation.surface: An author casts lots in a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks theatrical beside 'play', but it signals the rearrangement, giving LSTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Russian author of War and Peace and Anna Karenina.

clue.text: Ear, perhaps, for what's played in church

definitions.meaning: the ear is an example of a body part with a specific function
the pipe instrument heard at services

explanation.surface: A musician playing by ear in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a body part such as the ear, and the keyboard instrument with pipes in a church.

clue.text: US artifacts ace airman transported

indicators.note: transported means moved elsewhere, so the letters are carried into a new order

explanation.surface: A top pilot ferries American memorabilia.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective noun: objects and lore typical of American culture and history.

clue.text: Behind everyone else, in spite of everything

definitions.meaning: coming last of the lot, following the whole group

explanation.surface: Trailing the field yet persevering regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: literally following the whole group, and the idiom meaning nonetheless.

clue.text: Rise when clubs close

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a close is an end

explanation.surface: Getting up when the nightclubs shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to go up, climb or mount.
